notes:
Summary:
- Enterprise evaluation: dedicated GPU pool for low-latency customer-facing assistant + reranking pipeline. Primary ask = strict latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) for both streaming and non-streaming modes.
- Aim: deterministic tail latency under load with reserved capacity guarantees.

Technical requirements / quotes from call:
- "We need p95 < 120ms for non-streaming single-turn chat at 8 tokens/sec throughput per user, p99 < 220ms" — product lead.
- Streaming mode: client expects first-byte latency (time-to-first-chunk) p95 < 80ms, subsequent deltas < 25ms for 1–2 token chunk sizes.
- Throughput target for initial deployment: sustained 4k reqs/minute across 10 regions; burst to 12k/min for short windows.
- Model preference: quantized Llama-3 13B or equivalent; want fallbacks to smaller 7B for overflow.
- Data residency: US-only for analytics dataset. KMS must be used for key management.

Latency SLO definition & measurement alignment notes:
- Agreement needed on measurement points: client-side (SDK timestamp), edge proxy (ingress), server-side (runtime completion). Apexion insists on client-side for user-facing SLA, Redwood prefers edge-proxy + server-side for reproducibility.
- Proposed alignment: publish two SLOs — (1) User-facing SLO measured by client SDK (p50/p95/p99), sampled at 5% to limit telemetry costs; (2) Platform SLO measured at ingress+runtime for internal ops + billing.
- Define canonical timings:
  * client_request_start -> client_first_byte = time-to-first-chunk (streaming)
  * client_request_start -> client_last_byte = end-to-end latency (non-streaming & streaming full-response)
  * ingress_received -> runtime_complete = server processing latency
- Measurement delta handling: add explicit clock-drift tolerance (default 250ms) and require synchronized NTP within VPC images.
- Tail-latency accounting: p99 measured over 1-minute sliding windows, alert when p99 > configured SLO *and* sustained > 3 windows.

Instrumentation & test harness:
- Redwood will ship a small SDK patch to report client-side event markers (non-identifiable). SDK telemetry is opt-in for Apexion; default 5% sampling.
- Use Prometheus histograms at ingress and runtime; additionally produce aggregated percentile reports every 5 minutes.
- Tracing: include trace-id from client through edge to runtime; use Jaeger snapshot links in PoC artifacts.
- Load tests: two phases — synthetic baseline (no data ingress) then production-sim (realistic token lengths, KV cache warm). Expected run: 48 hours POC.

Reserved GPU planning / throughput guarantees:
- Redwood proposal: reserve 12 A100-equivalent slots for primary region (NYC), 4 on standby for autoscale-burst across regions. Expected throughput headroom computed from model perf: ~75 reqs/sec per slot for 13B quantized at 128-token avg.
- Apexion asks for hard throughput guarantee SLA for committed slots with a soft burst pool at 25% capacity for short spikes.
- Pricing ask: flat monthly reserved fee + token-overage pricing for bursts. Apexion requesting credit for SLA misses beyond 0.5% monthly violation.

SLA negotiation points / legal:
- Penalty model: Apexion prefers service credit proportional to missed p95/p99 hours. Redwood legal prefers capped credits and escalation windows.
- Requested additions: runbook-triggered reimbursements and rollback playbook for model fallback.

POC findings to date (Feb 28 run):
- Ingress-to-runtime p95 = 90ms; client-side measured p95 = 150ms (client network variability and SDK default sampling).
- Streaming time-to-first-chunk median = 58ms; p95 = 102ms.
- Under 2x load test (24-hour sustained), p99 spikes around 320ms on one region correlating with KV cache misses.
- Action: enable larger KV cache + adjust batching window to reduce tail.

Open action items / next steps:
- SE (Priya) to deliver measurement harness repo + Prometheus dashboards by 2026-03-10.
- Agree SLO billing boundary: finalize whether client-SDK SLO used for invoice credits (Apexion wants it). Redwood ops to propose middle-ground (edge-proxy canonical for credits).
- Legal to review proposed SLA credit formula (Apexion legal wants lower cap) — in progress.
- Schedule 1-hr negotiation with pricing + legal + engineering (target 2026-03-12).

Steno / quick notes from calls:
- "If you can't guarantee p99 under typical peaks we will fallback to multicloud strategy." — infra lead.
- Customer very sensitive to first-byte latency for conversational experience.
- Wants instrumentation to tie to user_id hashing for aggregated per-customer SLO reports (privacy-preserving).

Deal health & risks:
- Positive: strong product fit, willing to sign annual reserved contract if SLOs & credit terms acceptable.
- Risks: legal pushback on credit cap, customer insistence on client-side SLA boundary (hard to enforce and noisy), potential multi-region networking egress constraints that could raise cost.

Recommended Redwood internal notes:
- Prep a short doc comparing client-side vs ingress-based SLOs with cost and enforceability trade-offs (ops to own).
- Run a 24h trace-level capture during next PoC to identify outlier sources (network vs runtime).
- Consider offering a hybrid credit model: edge-proxy canonical for billing; client-side used for UX metrics and alarms.

Next visible milestone: SLO sign-off + measurement harness acceptance test (target 2026-03-15).
